Under the competitive-advantage assessment, continued support now yields 2 minus the proposal cost of 6, or -4. The coalition therefore decided not to support the federal proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Private commercial figures remain confidential.","candidate_implication":"In a larger documentary sample, withdrawals should be preceded by internal references to deteriorating competitive gains more often than by references to changes in alternative-regulation burdens.","derivation":"Under CA, support responds to incremental competitive benefit net of the common proposal cost. Only a competitive-benefit notice changes that payoff from positive to negative; decision and communication errors merely weaken the association.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can date and distinguish internal discussions of competitive gains from discussions of alternative-regulation burdens."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_01_02","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit to 2 while the expected burden of alternative regulation remained 12. Net of the proposal cost of 6, the relevant payoff is -4. The coalition decided to withdraw support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Private commercial assessments will not be disclosed.","candidate_implication":"When public statements conflict with internal records, subsequent confidential correspondence should usually continue to reflect the internally recorded decision rather than the public statement.","derivation":"The memo faithfully records the actual decision, whereas the public note can independently report its opposite. Thus disagreement makes the public communication error more likely than an undocumented decision change.","extra_assumption":"No new decision or materially relevant information intervenes between the public note and the subsequent confidential correspondence."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_01_03","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice reduced the expected burden of alternative regulation from 12 to 2 but left the incremental competitive benefit at 12. Under the competitive-advantage hypothesis, the relevant payoff remains 12 minus 6, or 6. The coalition decided to continue supporting the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Its private commercial calculations remain confidential.","candidate_implication":"Archived internal records should show that revisions to expected alternative-regulation burdens have little systematic effect on support when assessments of incremental competitive benefit remain unchanged.","derivation":"CA makes the support payoff depend on competitive benefit minus proposal cost, so a notice affecting only the alternative-regulation burden does not change the relevant payoff. The decision-reversal probability adds occasional exceptions.","extra_assumption":"The archive contains enough cases to distinguish systematic responsiveness from the independent decision errors."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_01_04","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private commercial notice revised the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2. Continued support would therefore produce a payoff of 2 minus the proposal cost of 6, equal to -4. The coalition decided not to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has withdrawn its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Confidential commercial estimates are not being released.","candidate_implication":"Internal documents immediately before withdrawal should contain negative net-benefit language more frequently than public withdrawal notes, which should tend to omit the underlying commercial quantities.","derivation":"The CA decision rule converts the private competitive estimate and proposal cost into the decision, while the public never directly receives the notice and private commercial numbers are not publicly disclosed.","extra_assumption":"Document authors normally record decision-relevant calculations internally when those calculations motivate a change in position."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_01_05","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice lowered the incremental competitive benefit from 12 to 2, making the CA payoff 2 minus 6, or -4. The ordinary rule points to ending support. Nevertheless, the coalition's realized decision reversed that prescription and retained support for the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Private commercial figures remain undisclosed.","candidate_implication":"A small minority of internal files should document decisions that run against their own recorded net competitive payoff, without requiring evidence that the underlying estimate changed again.","derivation":"The CA payoff rule ordinarily maps a negative payoff to nonsupport, but the independent 0.05 decision-reversal probability sometimes produces support despite the negative calculation.","extra_assumption":"Internal memoranda record both the payoff assessment and the realized decision rather than rationalizing the decision after the fact."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_01_06","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The reliable notice reduced the expected burden from alternative regulation to 2 but did not alter the incremental competitive benefit of 12. The CA payoff from continued support remains 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, or 6. The coalition decided to maintain support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition maintains its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal. It will not disclose private commercial estimates.","candidate_implication":"Internal discussions following burden-only notices should continue to calculate the proposal's attractiveness using competitive effects, even when the revised regulatory burden receives substantial discussion elsewhere in the file.","derivation":"The notice can change the alternative-regulation burden, but under CA only incremental competitive benefit enters the support payoff; with benefit 12 and cost 6, the decision rule still favors support.","extra_assumption":"Internal documents identify which consideration is treated as decision-relevant rather than merely recording both quantities without attribution."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_01_07","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice revised the incremental competitive benefit downward from 12 to 2, leaving the alternative-regulation burden unchanged. The relevant CA payoff is now -4 after subtracting the proposal cost of 6. The coalition decided to discontinue support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal. Confidential commercial assessments are not disclosed.","candidate_implication":"Across dated internal files, changes in coalition position should cluster after competitive-benefit revisions rather than merely after the passage of the day-10 information date.","derivation":"Both notice types arrive at the same time, but only the competitive-benefit notice changes the CA payoff's sign. Timing alone therefore cannot explain the predicted concentration of withdrawals by notice content.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can classify notice content and observe comparable cases receiving each notice type."},{"id":"confirmation_CA_01_08","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private notice lowered the expected incremental competitive benefit to 2. With the proposal cost fixed at 6, continued support has a CA payoff of -4. The expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12 but is not the operative criterion. The coalition decided not to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has ended its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal. No private commercial numbers will be released.","candidate_implication":"Researchers should find that internal justifications for position changes distinguish the operative competitive calculation from unchanged but salient regulatory exposure, whereas public notes reveal the position without that distinction.","derivation":"CA makes competitive benefit net of proposal cost operative, while the alternative-regulation burden can remain high without sustaining support. The public receives the decision but not the private commercial numbers.","extra_assumption":"Internal records preserve substantive justifications, and public-disclosure practices consistently protect the private inputs."}]}
